title: Graceful drain + token-bucket backpressure + lease sync for queue workers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple tenants experience intermittent p95/p99 spikes during rebalance and hot-shard conditions. Current worker lease & heartbeat handling plus nave prefetching causes long tail latency when a worker is force-evicted or when a consumer group rebalances. Retries currently amplify load because consumers immediately re-enqueue or aggressively prefetch, exacerbating stampedes on hot partitions.

Goals: 1) Reduce tail latency during graceful decommission and rebalances; 2) Provide a simple backpressure primitive per-worker and per-tenant that bounds inflight work; 3) Harmonize lease heartbeat semantics between Redis and Kafka workers so we can apply a single drain protocol; 4) Keep rollout low-risk with gradual opt-in flags and metrics.

Proposed approach:
- Introduce a token-bucket based inflight controller (worker-level) that caps concurrent processing and provides a soft-shed path when exhausted (return 429-ish internal and optionally requeue with jitter). This replaces current ad-hoc prefetch limits.
- Add a graceful-drain lifecycle to workers: on SIGTERM / pre-eviction signal start a Drain phase (stop taking new tokens, finish in-flight, extend short leases if needed), publish a short-lived drain marker to the coordination store for observability and routing.
- Synchronize lease/heartbeat semantics: create a small LeaseCoordinator abstraction used by both Redis lease workers and Kafka partition consumers to extend/renew leases in one consistent pattern. This enables the drain protocol to extend leases for short windows instead of immediate revocation.
- Adaptive retry shaping: when token bucket is exhausted, instead of immediate re-enqueue many times, workers should perform exponential-jitter requeue with bounded retries and push metrics to detect retry storms.
- Redis client upgrade: move to redis-client v7.x to gain optimized stream consumer features and pipelining improvements (benchmarked in staging).
- Telemetry & SLOs: add per-route inflight_gauge, drain_events, token_rejections, and retry_surfacing counters. Add synthetic test that simulates 10% hot-shard traffic under rebalance and assert p99 < target.

Acceptance criteria:
- New inflight controller in place for both Redis and Kafka consumers behind a feature flag.
- Graceful drain reduces requeue amplification observed in the synthetic workload by >60% and p99 latency reduced by >=25% in the test harness.
- No increase in missed messages during controlled shutdowns in staging.
- Rollout plan documented with kill-switch and metrics dashboards.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind tenant and binary-level switches. Deploy to canary infra with low-traffic tenants.
2) Run synthetic chaos (rebalance & evict) against canary and capture metrics.
3) If green, enable for more tenants in batches and monitor token_rejections and retry counts.
4) Full release tied to runtime-1.20 after 2 weeks of stable canary.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Mis-tuned token bucket could increase latency for some low-throughput tenants. Mitigation: default conservative settings and per-tenant overrides.
- Risk: Lease extension during drain may delay rebalancing if a machine is unhealthy. Mitigation: cap extension window (configurable) and expose drain markers for operators to force-evict.
- Risk: Redis client upgrade could introduce regressions. Mitigation: smoke tests, pinned staging run, and fallback to previous client via runtime flag.
comments: 2025-01-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after oncall incident where a single hot Redis stream caused a cascade of retries and p99 spikes. Referenced incident notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/incident-2025-01-hotstream

2025-01-14 Diego Martinez: Spike implemented for token-bucket inflight controller; initial microbench shows ~40% fewer requeues under artificial retry storm. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feat/token-bucket-spike

2025-01-18 Ruth Chen (Review): Concern about lease-extension delaying rebalancing for unhealthy nodes. Suggested bounded extension window and operator-visible drain marker. Added to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Graceful+Drain+Design

2025-01-22 Diego Martinez: Integrated LeaseCoordinator abstraction and wired into both RedisStreamConsumer and KafkaPartitionHandler. Local e2e tests pass. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213

2025-01-25 QA (Marcus Liu): Ran staging scenario with 50 tenants and simulated node eviction. Observed decrease in immediate re-enqueue by 63%, p99 reduced by ~28% for hot-shard flow. Noted two tenants with high retry_surfacing—investigating tenant-specific prefetch config.

2025-01-28 Performance (Jamal Kapoor): Benchmarked redis-client v7.x in staging: 12% improvement in stream consumer throughput and 6% lower median latency. Documented results in benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/redis-v7-bench

2025-01-30 Diego Martinez: Implemented feature flags: runtime.flag.inflight_controller and runtime.flag.graceful_drain. Added dashboard panels for token_rejections and drain_events. Preparing canary rollout and will open canary PR to ops runbook.
2025-02-03 Product (Lara Schmidt): Reviewed rollout plan; requested canary include at least one enterprise tenant and explicit rollback steps. Added release gating to release notes for runtime-1.20.
